title: prefetch-quota-smoothing-and-rollback-safepoint-hotfix
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: during a regional surge incident we observed cascading KV cache eviction spikes and sharp latency tails when prefetch attempts raced against aggressive tenant-level shedding. This PR implements a conservative prefetch quota smoothing heuristic plus a lightweight rollback-safepoint marker to avoid repeated failed prefetch attempts triggering cascading circuit flips. Goals: reduce tail P99 latency during short bursts, avoid repeated circuit reopen/close cycles, and provide an operational safepoint for emergency rollback without losing tenant state. Changes include a time-decayed prefetch budget per node, a soft-holdback period after consecutive prefetch failures, an explicit safepoint annotation that can be set by the control plane to freeze new prefetches, and a small guard in the SLO enforcer to prefer latency isolation over immediate eviction in transient conditions. The description below summarizes design, testing, rollout and rollback. Design summary: - Prefetch budget: each node tracks a decaying token bucket scoped to host-prefetch throughput; tokens refill slowly (configurable half-life) to prevent rapid rehydration after a spike. This avoids immediate re-issue of prefetches when load subsides. - Soft-holdback: after N (configurable, default 3) consecutive prefetch failures against remote KV or cold model shards, node enters a soft-holdback window where prefetches are deprioritized for T seconds. - Safepoint marker: control-plane can set a safepoint tag on a model/version which makes nodes skip prefetch initiation for that tagged model while preserving in-flight responses and KV eviction order. This enables emergency freezes during rolling upgrades. - SLO enforcer update: when node detects rising p95->p99 delta and prefetch budget is exhausted, the enforcer will prefer to return a slightly degraded but fast response (short-circuit with best-effort cached state) rather than trigger broad eviction that induces higher P99. Implementation notes: - service/slo/enforcer.go: add PrefetchBudgetChecker and logic path to signal graceful-degrade responses. - service/prefetch/prefetch_manager.go: new decay-based budget, soft-holdback state and metrics. - service/circuit/circuit_controller.go: integrate safepoint annotation evaluation before initiating prefetches; add short-circuit metrics for safepoint hits. - infra/k8s/helm/values.yaml: new feature flag prefetchBudget.enabled and tunables with safe defaults. - docs/operators/failover-runbook.md: documented how to flip safepoints from the control plane and runbook steps for incident responders. Tests & CI: unit tests added for budget decay math and holdback logic; integration tests simulate a regional surges with mocked remote KV failures and assert that P99 improves and that safepoint prevents new prefetch churn. Initial CI run showed an intermittent integration failure in the perf harness related to timing; test flakiness was fixed by switching to a wall-clock tolerant assertion and adding a short retry. See ci_checks for details. Rollout plan: - Feature behind feature-flag (prefetchBudget.enabled) default off for all clusters. - Canary: enable in a single low-traffic region for 1 hour with strict telemetry (p50/p95/p99, prefetch-failures, circuit-flips). - Gradual ramp: if canary shows <5% P99 regression and prefetch-failures drop by >30% on surge simulation, roll to other regions. - Operator safepoint: customers/operators can set safepoint tag to stop prefetching for a model at any time; included in runbook. Rollback plan: - Flip the k8s feature flag off (immediate) which disables new budget checks and holdbacks; nodes will gracefully resume prior prefetch behavior after budget drains (max additional prefetches bounded). - If an emergency revert is required, the safepoint marker can be set to freeze prefetching while a patch is staged. Observability & metrics added: prefetch.tokens, prefetch.holdback_count, prefetch.safepoint_hits, slo.prefetch_degrade_count, slo.prefetch_degrade_latency_delta. Suggested alerting thresholds included in docs/operators/failover-runbook.md. Security & compliance: no new external network paths. Safepoint tag is write-restricted to control-plane API role; annotations validated server-side. Related work items: ENG-4321 (prefetch stability), SUP-1187 (support ticket for incident 2024-04-29), follow-up ENG-4432 (tune half-life defaults).
